summary: Checked all 63 requested records: 56 estimates, six study records and the paper-level supplement metadata/change log. Read both complete markdown conversions, including the main Reporting Summary, all ten main-PDF pages and all eight supplement-PDF pages; recovered Supplementary Table 1 cells with pymupdf.find_tables to check row and page continuations. Also checked the original Lee and Chung methods, PDF pp. 6-8, for inherited assignment and submission structure. Found six instances of one coding error: all S1 estimates use se_basis=output although the reanalysis has one whole submission per participant. Read the local author notebook without executing it and checked its Study 1 input files against the cleaned participant submissions to resolve the multiple-ideas ambiguity. No published effect, uncertainty statistic or participant count was recalculated or replaced with a data-derived value. All recorded numerical values match the cited PDF text and the correct outcome, arm contrast and table row. Study and arm counts belong to the reanalysis; unprinted contrast totals and S6 arm counts remain null. The S3 table-wide total includes a model-only pool and is correctly not recorded as a people total. The other reviewed question, construct, measure, unit, direction, AI-availability, timing, within-person, comparison-type, uncertainty-basis and preregistered-primary codes are consistent with the sources and codebook. The 185 supplement_changes entries agree with the current file. All 14 pre-existing numerical statistical entries remain unchanged and match the main PDF: nine confidence levels, the S3 control percentage and the four stored sprinkler counts. The 45 added estimates are distinct eligible robustness contrasts. The descending S2 MST interval, malformed interval brackets, rounded-percentage/risk-difference discrepancies and printed p-values are source issues already documented in the extraction; they were not treated as transcription errors. Signed similarity coefficients retain their documented control-minus-treatment direction, and percentage arm levels remain distinct from proportion-scale risk differences. Only the requested verification JSON was written.
